rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s permission to divorce during any part of a nonconsummated purity, without specifying its beginning or end, is evidence against al-Zuhri’s timing restriction.
rows.anchor: والحجة على الزهري أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أذن في طلاق الطاهر من غير جماع

rows.speaker: أشهب
rows.claim: Ashhab says the marital bond and inheritance continue until the blood is confirmed as menstruation, so a nonmenstrual discharge is not mistaken for it.
rows.anchor: وقال أشهب: لا تنقطع العصمة والميراث حتى يتحقق أنه دم حيض

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Kufans cite the Prophet’s instruction to Fatima bint Abi Hubaysh: treat the bleeding as a vein, stop praying at menstruation, then purify and pray between periods.
rows.anchor: احتج الكوفيون بقوله عليه السلام لفاطمة بنت أبي حبيش حين شكت إليه الدم

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans infer from 65:4, which names menstruation as what women may despair of and assigns months in its absence, that menstruation is the waiting-period measure.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى: واللائي يئسن من المحيض من نسآئكم إن ارتبتم فعدتهن ثلاثة أشهر

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar said before the Companions that a slave woman’s waiting period is two menstruations, half the free woman’s; he would have made it one and a half if possible.
rows.anchor: وقال عمربحضرة الصحابة: عدة الأمة حيضتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because no Companion objected to Umar, al-Qurtubi treats his ruling as consensus, supported by ten Companions including the four caliphs.
rows.anchor: فدل على أنه إجماع منهم وهو قول عشرة من الصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi reads the three quruʾ as three complete menstrual periods: a purity-based count could include the remainder of the purity in which divorce occurred, then only part of another.
rows.anchor: يريد كوامل، وهذا لا يمكن أن يكون إلا على قولنا بأن الأقراء الحيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On his view, a woman divorced during an unconsummated purity starts at the next menstruation, counts three periods, and leaves the waiting period after bathing from the third.
rows.anchor: فإذا طلق الرجل المرأة في طهر لم يطأ فيه استقبلت حيضة ثم حيضة ثم حيضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He invokes the grammatical gender of quruʾ alongside masculine ayyām in 69:7 as a response in the debate over the intended sense of quruʾ.
rows.anchor: لأن اليوم مذكر وكذلك القرء فدل على أنه المراد

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa agrees that a woman divorced while menstruating does not count that menstruation or the following purity, but begins with the menstruation after that purity; al-Qurtubi instead counts the purity.
rows.anchor: ووافقنا أبو حنيفة على أنها إذا طلقت حائضا أنها لا تعتد بالحيضة التي طلقت فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic may use a plural time expression for a partial total: 2:197 calls the pilgrimage months, though the period is two months and part of a third, so three quruʾ can likewise include partial units.
rows.anchor: وقد استجاز أهل اللغة أن يعبروا عن البعض باسم الجميع كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase in 2:197, “pilgrimage months,” refers to two months and part of a third, illustrating plural wording for a partial amount.
rows.anchor: والمراد به شهران وبعض الثالث فكذلك قوله

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Among scholars who take quruʾ as menstruations, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Tawus, Ibn Shubruma, and al-Awzaʿi say the waiting period ends after bathing from the third period, when revocation also ends.
rows.anchor: قاله سعيد ابن جبير وطاوس وابن شبرمة والأوزاعي

rows.speaker: شريك
rows.claim: Sharik says that even if a woman delays bathing for twenty years, her husband retains the right of revocation until she bathes.
rows.anchor: وقال شريك: إذا فرطت المرأة في الغسل عشرين سنة فلزوجها عليها الرجعة

rows.speaker: إسحاق بن راهويه
rows.claim: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh says that entering the third menstruation ends the marriage bond and revocation right, though she may not marry until bathing from it.
rows.anchor: وروي عن إسحاق بن راهويه أنه قال: إذا طعنت المرأة في الحيضة الثالثة بانت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A similar position is attributed to Ibn Abbas, but al-Qurtubi calls it weak and counters it with 2:234, where reaching the term precedes freedom to act about oneself.
rows.anchor: وروي نحوه عن ابن عباس وهو قول ضعيف، بدليل قول الله تعالى:

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi counts the transition from purity into menstruation as a quruʾ, shortening the waiting period: a divorce at the very end of purity is counted at once, and transition into the third ends the bond.
rows.anchor: وأما ما ذكره الشافعي من أن نفس الانتقال من الطهر إلى الحيضة يسمى قرءا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority of scholars hold that a menstruating slave woman waits two menstrual periods after divorce.
rows.anchor: والجمهور من العلماء على أن عدة الأمة التي تحيض من طلاق زوجها حيضتان

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin says he would regard a slave woman’s waiting period as the same as a free woman’s unless a Prophetic practice established otherwise, since the practice deserves following.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن سيرين أنه قال: ما أرى عدة الأمة إلا كعدة الحرة

rows.speaker: الأصم عبد الرحمن بن كيسان وداود بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Asamm Abd al-Rahman ibn Kaysan, Dawud ibn Ali, and other literalists say the waiting-period verses apply equally to slave and free women.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصم عبد الرحمن بن كيسان وداود بن علي وجماعة أهل الظاهر: إن الآيات في عدة الطلاق

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The majority cite a report from Aisha that the divorce allotment for a slave woman is two and her quruʾ are two menstruations; al-Qurtubi notes that Mazahir ibn Aslam alone transmitted it and is weak.
rows.anchor: عن القاسم بن محمد عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar is reported to have said that whichever spouse is enslaved reduces the divorce allotment; a group of scholars followed him.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر: أيهما رق نقص طلاقه وقالت به فرقة من العلماء

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima, al-Zuhri, and al-Nakhaʿi interpret what is in the wombs as menstruation.
rows.anchor: أي من الحيض قاله عكرمة والزهري والنخعي

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar and Ibn Abbas interpret what is in the wombs as pregnancy.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الحمل قاله عمر وابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the phrase includes both menstruation and pregnancy, on the premise that a pregnant woman can menstruate.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الحيض والحمل معا وهذا على أن الحامل تحيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because only women know their menstruation or purity and the waiting period depends on it, their statement about its ending or continuation is accepted and they are entrusted with disclosure.
rows.anchor: جعل القول قولها إذا ادعت انقضاء العدة أو عدمها، وجعلهن مؤتمنات على ذلك

rows.speaker: سليمان بن يسار
rows.claim: Sulayman ibn Yasar says people were not ordered to inspect women’s private parts; the matter was entrusted to women as persons trusted to report it.
rows.anchor: وقال سليمان بن يسار: ولم نؤمر أن نفتح النساء فننظر إلى فروجهن، ولكن وكل ذلك إليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on concealment protects the husband: falsely claiming menstruation removes his revocation right; falsely denying it can impose extra maintenance or prevent revocation until the term expires; concealing pregnancy can likewise block his right.
rows.anchor: ومعنى النهي عن الكتمان النهي عن الإضرار بالزوج وإذهاب حقه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the verse was revealed because women in pre-Islamic times concealed pregnancy so they could attribute the child to a new husband.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: كانت عادتهن في الجاهلية أن يكتمن الحمل ليلحقن الولد بالزوج الجديد

rows.speaker: رجل من أشجع
rows.claim: A man from Ashjaʿ told the Prophet he feared his divorced pregnant wife might remarry and the child be attributed to another man; the verse was revealed and the Ashjaʿi woman returned to him.
rows.anchor: وحكي أن رجلا من أشجع أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله، إني طلقت

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says the scholars known to him reject a claim of three periods and completed waiting period within ten days, unless the woman says she miscarried a fetus with discernible form.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: وقال كل من حفظت عنه من أهل العلم: إذا قالت المرأة في عشرة أيام

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik accepts a claim of completed waiting period when the stated duration is one in which it could normally end; if the duration is exceptionally rare, he reports two opinions.
rows.anchor: فقال مالك: إذا قالت انقضت عدتي في أمد تنقضي في مثله العدة قبل قولها

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: In the Mudawwana, Malik accepts a claim of three periods in a month if women confirm it; Shurayh agrees, and Ali praised Shurayh’s judgment.
rows.anchor: قال في المدونة: إذا قالت حضت ثلاث حيض في شهر صدقت إذا صدقها النساء

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali told Shurayh “qālūn,” meaning he had judged correctly and well, on accepting a woman’s claim when other women corroborated it.
rows.anchor: قال له علي بن أبي طالب: قالون! أي أصبت وأحسنت

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: In Muhammad’s book, the woman is not believed to have completed the three periods in less than a month and a half.
rows.anchor: وقال في كتاب محمد: لا تصدق إلا في شهر ونصف

rows.speaker: أبو ثور
rows.claim: Abu Thawr sets the minimum at forty-seven days, reasoning from a minimum purity of fifteen days and a minimum menstruation of one day.
rows.anchor: قال أبو ثور: أقل ما يكون ذلك في سبعة وأربعين يوما

rows.speaker: النعمان
rows.claim: Al-Nuʿman and al-Shafiʿi do not believe a claim of completed waiting period in less than sixty days.
rows.anchor: وقال النعمان: لا تصدق في أقل من ستين يوما وقال به الشافعي

words: إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional is a severe warning that reinforces the ban on concealment and the duty to state truthfully what is in the womb.
rows.anchor: هذا وعيد عظيم شديد لتأكيد تحريم الكتمان، وإيجاب لأداء الأمانة

words: إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional does not imply that unbelievers may conceal; like “if you are my brother, do not wrong me,” it means faith should keep a person from such conduct.
rows.anchor: على أنه أبيح لمن لا يؤمن أن يكتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿūla is the plural of baʿl, “husband”; he is so called for his elevation over the wife through the marital rights he possesses.
rows.anchor: البعولة جمع البعل، وهو الزوج سمي بعلا لعلوه على الزوجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word baʿl also means lord because of elevation in lordship, as in 37:125, where it refers to a deity addressed as lord.
rows.anchor: أي ربا لعلوه في الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿl has the plural baʿūla like dhakar/dhukūra and faḥl/fuḥūla; the group feminine ending is emphatic and irregular, so its use is attested rather than extended by analogy, though it may instead be a feminine ending on faʿūl.
rows.anchor: وهذه الهاء زائدة مؤكدة لتأنيث الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿūla can also be a verbal noun; baʿala means to become a husband, while mubāʿala and biʿāl mean intercourse, and a man is his wife’s baʿl while she is his baʿla.
rows.anchor: فالرجل بعل المرأة، والمرأة بعلته

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet described the days of Tashriq as days of eating, drinking, and intercourse.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام لأيام التشريق: «إنها أيام أكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿl can also mean the owner or master of something.
rows.anchor: وفلان بعل هذا أي مالكه وربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “returning them” means taking them back in revocation; he distinguishes revocation during the waiting period, linked to Ibn Umar, from return after it, linked to Maʿqil.
rows.anchor: أي بمراجعتهن فالمراجعة على ضربين: مراجعة في العدة على حديث ابن عمر. ومراجعة بعد العدة على حديث معقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general waiting-period clause covers all divorced women, including those divorced three times and those divorced fewer; the right of husbands to revoke is specifically for the latter.
rows.anchor: حكم خاص فيمن كان طلاقها دون الثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is consensus that a free husband may revoke a consummated wife after one or two divorces during her waiting period even against her will; after it expires, she is independent and can return only through a new proposal and marriage with guardian and witnesses.
rows.anchor: أنه أحق برجعتها ما لم تنقض عدتها وإن كرهت المرأة

rows.speaker: المهلب
rows.claim: Al-Muhallab says revocation during the waiting period requires no marriage formalities beyond witnesses to the revocation, a consensus he links to 65:2, which mentions witnesses for revocation but not for marriage or divorce.
rows.anchor: قال المهلب: وكل من راجع في العدة

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says the Qurʾanic evidence cited together with scholarly consensus suffices, without recounting earlier reports on the subject.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: وفيما ذكرناه من كتاب الله

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik counts intercourse during the waiting period as revocation when he intends to return her, even without witnesses; the wife should prevent intercourse until he witnesses, and Ishaq agrees.
rows.anchor: فقال مالك: إذا وطئها في العدة وهو يريد الرجعة وجهل أن يشهد فهي رجعة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Malik’s intention-based rule cites the Prophetic report that deeds are judged by intentions and each person receives according to what he intended.
rows.anchor: إنما الأعمال بالنيات وإنما لكل امرىء ما نوى

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: When intercourse occurs without intending revocation, Malik says the husband may revoke during the waiting period but must not have intercourse again until she has completed an interval to establish that his unlawful semen is cleared.
rows.anchor: قال مالك: يراجع في العدة ولا يطأ حتى يستبرئها

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says that after the waiting period she cannot marry her former husband or another man during the remaining clearance period; a marriage then is annulled, but does not create permanent prohibition because the semen was his.
rows.anchor: قال ابن القاسم: فإن انقضت عدتها لم ينكحها هو ولا غيره في بقية مدة الاستبراء

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibn Sirin, al-Zuhri, Ata, Tawus, and al-Thawri hold that intercourse itself is revocation; witnesses should be used, as held also by the Hanafi school, al-Awzaʿi, and Ibn Abi Layla.
rows.anchor: هكذا قال سعيد بن المسيب والحسن البصري وابن سيرين والزهري

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abu Umar reports a view among some Maliki authorities that intercourse revokes in every case, whether intended or not; al-Layth adopted it.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمر: وقد قيل: وطؤه مراجعة على كل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that a seller with an option to cancel a slave-girl sale can have intercourse during the option period, thereby reclaiming her and undoing the sale; the author says a revocable wife has the same status.
rows.anchor: ولم يختلفوا فيمن باع جاريته بالخيار أن له وطأها في مدة الخيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kiss or other intimate touch with intent to revoke counts as revocation; without that intent, kissing or touching is sinful but does not constitute revocation.
rows.anchor: من قبل أو باشر ينوي بذلك الرجعة كانت رجعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sunnah is to witness revocation before intercourse, kissing, or intimate touching.
rows.anchor: والسنة أن يشهد قبل أن يطأ أو قبل أن يقبل أو يباشر

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa, his companions, and al-Thawri count intercourse, lustful touching, or looking at her private parts with desire as revocation; they recommend witnesses.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه: إن وطئها أو لمسها بشهوة

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik, al-Shafiʿi, Ishaq, Abu Ubayd, and Abu Thawr say these acts do not constitute revocation.
rows.anchor: وفي قول مالك والشافعي وإسحاق وأبي عبيد وأبي ثور لا يكون رجعة

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
rows.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Muhammad says revocation is valid by intercourse, a kiss, and all other forms of sexual enjoyment, while speech-based revocation is undisputed.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف في صحة الارتجاع بالقول فأما بالفعل نحو الجماع والقبلة فقال القاضي أبو محمد

rows.speaker: ابن المواز
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mawwaz includes pleasurable touching and looking at her private parts or nearby beauty when done intending revocation; this differs from al-Shafiʿi’s speech-only rule, also attributed to Abu Thawr, Jabir ibn Zayd, and Abu Qilaba.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المواز: ومثل الجسة للذة، أو أن ينظر إلى فرجها

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik and al-Shafiʿi do not allow the husband to travel with a revocable wife until he revokes; Abu Hanifa and his companions allow travel before revocation.
rows.anchor: فقال مالك والشافعي: لا يسافر بها حتى يراجعها

rows.speaker: زفر
rows.claim: Reports from Zufar differ: al-Hasan ibn Ziyad transmits permission to travel before revocation, while Amr ibn Khalid transmits that travel must wait until revocation.
rows.anchor: إلا زفر فإنه روى عنه الحسن بن زياد أن له

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik says he must not be alone with her or enter without permission; she remains covered, he may not see her hair, they may eat together if someone else is present, but not sleep together in one room.
rows.anchor: فقال مالك. لا يخلو معها

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says Malik later retracted the permission to enter, maintaining that the husband may not enter or see her hair.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن القاسم: رجع مالك عن ذلك فقال: لا يدخل عليها

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and his companions agree that the revocable wife may adorn herself for her husband with perfume, jewelry, and dress.
rows.anchor: ولم يختلف أبو حنيفة وأصحابه في أنها تتزين له وتتطيب وتلبس الحلي

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab says she should ask permission, may wear clothes and jewelry, and if they share one house they should separate with a curtain; Qatada also recommends announcing entry with a greeting and throat-clearing.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن المسيب قال إذا طلق الرجل امرأته تطليقة فإنه يستأذن عليها

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi treats a revocably divorced wife as forbidden to her former husband like an irrevocably divorced woman until he revokes, and holds that revocation requires spoken words.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: المطلقة طلاقا يملك رجعتها محرمة على مطلقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By consensus, after the waiting period ends, if a husband says he revoked during it and the wife denies this, her statement with an oath prevails and he cannot take her back on that basis.
rows.anchor: أجمع العلماء على أن المطلق إذا قال بعد انقضاء العدة: إني كنت راجعتك في العدة وأنكرت

rows.speaker: النعمان
rows.claim: Al-Nuʿman does not require an oath in disputes about marriage or revocation; his two companions agree with the rest of scholars that an oath is required.
rows.anchor: غير أن النعمان كان لا يرى يمينا في النكاح ولا في الرجعة وخالفه صاحباه

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: If an enslaved wife denies her husband’s claim of revocation after the waiting period, her statement prevails even if her master calls her a liar, according to al-Shafiʿi, Abu Thawr, and al-Nuʿman.
rows.anchor: هذا قول الشافعي وأبي ثور والنعمان

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaqub and Muhammad say the master’s claim prevails in a dispute over a slave wife’s revocation and that the master has the stronger claim to her.
rows.anchor: وقال يعقوب ومحمد: القول قول المولى وهو أحق بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word “return” implies that the marital bond was removed; al-Qurtubi’s school says intercourse is forbidden to the revocably divorced woman, so return restores permissibility.
rows.anchor: لفظ الرد يقتضي زوال العصمة إلا أن علماءنا قالوا: إن الرجعية محرمة الوطء

rows.speaker: الليث بن سعد
rows.claim: Al-Layth, Abu Hanifa, and their followers say marital rulings remain intact and divorce only reduces the allotted number; revocation turns the wife back from the path toward separation as the waiting period expires, a figurative return.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث بن سعد وأبو حنيفة ومن قال بقولهما في أن الرجعة محللة الوطء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi distinguishes his school’s literal return: intercourse has actually become forbidden, so revocation restores a real, presently lost permission.
rows.anchor: والرد الذي حكمنا به رد حقيقي فإن هناك زوال مستنجز وهو تحريم الوطء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “More entitled” is used when two rights compete and one prevails: the husband’s right during the waiting period exceeds her right to herself, which begins only after it ends.
rows.anchor: يطلق عند تعارض حقين، ويترجح أحدهما فالمعنى حق الزوج

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The author compares the phrasing to the Prophetic statement that a previously married woman is more entitled to herself than her guardian.
rows.anchor: ومثل هذا قوله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revocation is commendable when intended to repair the relationship and remove estrangement; using it to harm the wife, prolong her waiting, or prevent her release is forbidden under 2:231, though the revocation remains valid and a judge may separate them if the intent is known.
rows.anchor: فأما إذا قصد الإضرار وتطويل العدة والقطع بها عن الخلاص من ربقة النكاح فمحرم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says wives have marital rights corresponding to those husbands have over them; he adorns himself for his wife and does not take every right, so she can claim hers, with adornment kept free of sin.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إني لأتزين لامرأتي كما تتزين لي، وما أحب أن أستنظف كل حقي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also explains that wives receive good companionship and kind treatment from husbands just as they owe the obedience Allah has required of them.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا: أي لهن من حسن الصحبة والعشرة بالمعروف على أزواجهن مثل الذي عليهن

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says a wife’s rights include her husband refraining from harming her, just as she must not harm him.
rows.anchor: كما كان ذلك عليهن لأزواجهن. قاله الطبري

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says husbands should fear God concerning their wives just as wives should fear God concerning their husbands; the author says the meanings are close.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: تتقون الله فيهن كما عليهن أن يتقين الله عز وجل فيكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse comprehensively includes all rights within marriage.
rows.anchor: والآية تعم جميع ذلك من حقوق الزوجية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars explain Ibn Abbas’s self-adornment as matching one’s appearance to age, time, and suitability: a trimmed mustache can suit an older man but look poor on a young man without a full beard.
rows.anchor: زينة تليق بالشباب، وزينة تليق بالشيوخ

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet said that God commanded him to let his beard grow and trim his mustache.
rows.anchor: وروي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Men’s adornment also includes suitable clothing and, depending on the individual, kohl; perfume, tooth-cleaning, grooming, purification, and nail-clipping suit everyone, with henna for older men and rings for men of all ages.
rows.anchor: فأما الطيب والسواك والخلال والرمي بالدرن وفضول الشعر والتطهير وقلم الأظفار فهو بين موافق للجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A husband should adorn himself in a fitting way to please his wife and help preserve her chastity, and attend to her sexual needs; if unable to fulfill her in bed, he should take medicines that increase potency and desire.
rows.anchor: ليكون عند امرأته في زينة تسرها ويعفها عن غيره من الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daraja means rank or status; the author also connects its root to a road’s edge, traversing one’s lifetime, stairs, and strength-related words such as rajul and rajīl.
rows.anchor: مدرجة الطريق: قارعته والأصل فيه الطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man’s additional degree lies in intellect, strength, financial support, blood money, inheritance, and jihad.
rows.anchor: فزيادة درجة الرجل بعقله وقوته وبالإنفاق وبالدية والميراث والجهاد

rows.speaker: حميد
rows.claim: Humayd is reported to interpret the degree as the beard; al-Qurtubi says this, if correctly attributed, is weak and unsupported by the wording or meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال حميد: الدرجة اللحية وهذا إن صح عنه فهو ضعيف

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi claims men’s superiority is clear, citing woman’s creation from man and the husband’s authority over her actions, fasting, and pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: فطوبى لعبد أمسك عما لا يعلم

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi interprets the degree as the bridal payment.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الدرجة الصداق قاله الشعبي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation takes the degree to mean the permissibility of disciplining a wife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جواز الأدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In sum, the degree indicates preference and that the husband’s right over his wife is more binding than hers over him.
rows.anchor: وعلى الجملة فدرجة تقتضي التفضيل، وتشعر بأن حق الزوج عليها أوجب من حقها عليه

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet said that if he were to command anyone to prostrate to another besides God, he would command a wife to prostrate to her husband.
rows.anchor: ولو أمرت أحدا بالسجود لغير الله لأمرت المرأة أن تسجد لزوجها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the degree as an exhortation for men to show good companionship and generosity toward women; Ibn Atiyya calls this a fine and excellent interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الدرجة إشارة إلى حض الرجال على حسن العشرة، والتوسع للنساء في المال

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi suggests the degree concerns marital rights: the husband can end the marriage, whereas the wife cannot, and she must answer his call to bed though he is not likewise obliged.
rows.anchor: قال الماوردي، يحتمل أنها في حقوق النكاح له رفع العقد دونها

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet warned that angels curse a woman who refuses her husband’s call to bed until morning.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا قوله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aziz means that God’s sovereignty is invincible and unchallenged; al-Hakim means He knows and acts rightly.
rows.anchor: أي منيع السلطان لا معترض عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “if you fear” refers to fear that is alarm or panic.
rows.anchor: من الخوف الذي هو الفزع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farijālan means pray on foot; a person is called rajil or rājil when walking because he has no mount, and the passage lists several Arabic singular and plural forms.
rows.anchor: والرجال جمع راجل أو رجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase aw rukbānan is coordinated with farijālan; rajil and rājil are forms for a person walking, with multiple plural forms cited from al-Tabari and others.
rows.anchor: رجل الإنسان يرجل رجلا إذا عدم المركوب ومشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding prayer with calm, stillness, and composure in the usual safe condition, God addresses occasional danger and makes clear that prayer never falls away; He permits prayer on foot or mounted, with gestures of the head, in any direction.
rows.anchor: ذكر حالة الخوف الطارئة أحيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This concession covers an isolated worshipper whose life is endangered by combat, a pursuing beast or enemy, a flood, or any other imminent threat to life.
rows.anchor: وهذه هي صلاة الفذ الذي قد ضايقه الخوف على نفسه في حال المسايفة أو من سبع يطلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that in this danger concession a person may face whichever direction and move or turn as needed to save himself.
rows.anchor: هذه الرخصة في ضمنها إجماع العلماء أن يكون الإنسان حيثما توجه من السموت ويتقلب ويتصرف

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi limits this prayer to serious enemy danger: the forces see each other and Muslims are exposed to weapons, or a reliable messenger reports an enemy approaching rapidly; otherwise the concession does not apply.
rows.anchor: فقال الشافعي: هو إطلال العدو عليهم

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: If Muslims pray the danger prayer on reliable news that the enemy is near and the enemy then leaves, Abu Hanifa says they must repeat it; another opinion says no repetition is due.
rows.anchor: يعيدون وهو قول أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abu Umar distinguishes the severe-danger prayer here, which may be on foot or mounted and with or without facing the qibla, from the congregational prayer of fear led by an imam, whose rules are treated in Surat al-Nisaʾ.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمر: فالحال التي يجوز منها للخائف أن يصلي راجلا أو راكبا

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik distinguishes fear of a fighting enemy from threats such as a beast or flood; if nonenemy danger passes, he recommends repeating the prayer within its time, while most jurists treat the cases alike.
rows.anchor: وفرق مالك بين خوف العدو المقاتل وبين خوف السبع ونحوه من جمل صائل أو سيل

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa says fighting invalidates prayer; al-Qurtubi says the Ibn Umar report contradicts him and the verse’s plain sense is stronger evidence against him.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة: إن القتال يفسد الصلاة
